research_rationale: EO 10587 (signed 1955-01-13, 20 FR 361; Trading with the Enemy Act sec. 32(h)), read in full from the held FR text, has three operative sections (designation of the Jewish Restitution Successor Organization, delegation to the Attorney General, power to subdelegate) and no term or sunset. The dossier inventory omitted sec. 1, so the inventory is corrected by overrides to secs. 1-3. EO 11086 (1963-02-26, 28 FR 1833, held official text) restated all three sections: sec. 1 in substance unchanged (a partial amendment, attached), secs. 2 and 3 replaced by different texts, so the original words of secs. 2 and 3 ended on 1963-02-26. The order as amended ran until EO 12553 revoked it: EO 12553 revokes EO 10587 'and any amendments thereto' and also lists EO 11086 in its own row. EO 12553 (51 FR 7237, signed February 25, 1986; held official FR text, text sha256 6361bdc5...) says 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked' and lists the order in its 'No. Subject' table; it has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is READ as effective on signing, the on_signing reading 1986-02-25 (FR publication 1986-03-03 is not an effective date); this date is an upper bound, not a certified end. Sec. 1 is the last clause to end, so the whole-order end is the on_signing reading 1986-02-25. EO 11086 is not the whole-order end because it left sec. 1 in force. Earlier-end test: the OFR catalog, U.S. Code and eCFR searches show only EO 11086 and EO 12553; a number search of the held fr-originals texts finds no other order naming EO 10587. Statutory leads (Pub. L. 87-846 sec. 204(a) rewrote sec. 32(h); the programme's later lapse) are not held as text, are not express ends of this order's sec. 1 and are recorded only as context. No report deadline or other unheld date is needed for any clause's first end here; the discharge-conditioned text of restated sec. 3 belongs to EO 11086.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12553 (EO 12553, 51 FR 7237, read once in full): one operative sentence revoking the listed orders 'and any amendments thereto', no savings, continuation, transfer, exception or delayed-effect wording, so EO 12553 saves and transfers nothing. Own-residual check, reading EO 10587 and EO 11086 in full: EO 10587 designated the Jewish Restitution Successor Organization as successor in interest under sec. 32(h) of the Trading with the Enemy Act and delegated the President's sec. 32(h) functions (first to the Attorney General, from 1963 to the Foreign Claims Settlement Commission, with the Attorney General keeping jurisdiction over claims filed before the 1962 amendment). A completed designation, claims filed by the organization and payments or discharges made under the delegated functions are accrued effects that rest on the statute and on completed acts, not on the revoked order, and nothing in EO 12553 undoes them. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (1961-01-17, effective on filing for publication, 1961-01-18; 26 FR 508): returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by the listed chapters of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 'shall be open to inspection by certain classes of persons and State and Federal Government establishments' under the Treasury decision approved the same day; the last paragraph supersedes EO 10738 of 1957-11-15 to the extent it applied to inspection by State tax officials of estate and gift-tax returns. The dossier splits this text into a clause and a fragment ('1954.'); the override restates it as one clause covering both paragraphs. No term, sunset, condition or report date. EO 10954 amended the last paragraph (attached). EO 10738, which EO 10906 supersedes in part, is itself in the EO 12553 number list, so there is no revival question. Lead recorded, not an express end: the Tax Reform Act of 1976 rewrote sec. 6103 of the Internal Revenue Code and may have displaced the inspection-by-order system before 1986; no statutory text is held, the OLRC note at 26 U.S.C. 6103 note (which lists this order and says EO 12553 revoked it) does not record any earlier statutory ending, and a statutory displacement is not an express end, so EO 12553 is the first express end and the date is an upper bound.

It has no own-terms end. EO 10954 (1961-07-26, effective as of 1961-01-18, held official text) restated the last paragraph; attached. EO 12553 (51 FR 7237, signed February 25, 1986; held official FR text, text sha256 6361bdc5...) says 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked' and lists the order in its 'No. Subject' table; it has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is READ as effective on signing, the on_signing reading 1986-02-25 (FR publication 1986-03-03 is not an effective date); this date is an upper bound, not a certified end. EO 10954 is also listed in EO 12553's table, so the amending order is ended by its own row. Earlier-end test: OFR catalog, U.S. Code and eCFR show only EO 10954, EO 10738 (superseded in part by this order, not the reverse) and EO 12553; no other held order names EO 10906. The Tax Reform Act of 1976 rewrite of IRC 6103 is an unheld statutory lead, recorded and not treated as an express end; the claim's end is therefore an upper bound on the on_signing reading.
